quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: Highway signs that warn about dangerous conditions are called:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to dangerous conditions ahead. Always obey warning signs for your safety. Ignoring a warning sign can cause accidents.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
questions.explanation: Always begin signaling about 100 feet before you turn left. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. Always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: You may drive slower than the posted speed limit when conditions require it, but never faster. Reduce speed for curves, hills with limited visibility, slippery roads, and areas with animals or pedestrians.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren. Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You should stop for other traffic.
Traffic is entering from another road. Give them extra space to merge safely into traffic.
Traffic is entering from another road and you should keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is entering from another road. Give them extra space to merge safely into traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is merging into your lane. Check your side and rear mirrors, then move to another lane if possible to let merging drivers through safely.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. You should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Release the accelerator and slow down gradually. When moving very slowly, apply brakes lightly and pull to a safe area.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and drive through it.
Put the car in neutral while driving through the water.

questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles to prevent skidding. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition with enough tread.
Keep your tires at the right air pressure.

questions.explanation: Prevent hydroplaning by keeping tire tread in good condition and maintaining proper tire pressure. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: Fog reduces your ability to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see better.

questions.explanation: In fog, drive slowly and carefully. Do not use high beams. Low beams light up the road and objects better in fog.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, look both ways, and only drive when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Which one is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using your high beam lights in fog.
Staring straight ahead at the road.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors every two to five seconds to watch for hazards. Staring only ahead is unsafe. In fog, use low beams, not high beams.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with more than one lane in your direction, you should:

options.text: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.
Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane nearest to where you came from. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane when:

options.text: The driver you passed signals for you to return.
You see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you are not too close to the vehicle you just passed. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return to your lane.

questions.question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Keep driving at the same speed in your lane.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to give the emergency vehicle space. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down below the speed limit and give it as much room as possible. Always be ready to stop at emergency scenes.

questions.question: Reaction time is slower after:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your vision, makes you less alert, and worsens your judgment. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and how other vehicles are moving.

questions.question: It is best to keep a space cushion:

options.text: Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left and right.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear soon.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will come next.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed where it is posted.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as well. Keep more distance between you and the car ahead so you have time to stop if it stops suddenly. Use your headlights correctly, switching between high and low beams as needed.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before going.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the train passes.
Go when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before going.
questions.explanation: Do not start moving as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before you cross. Check again for another train that may be coming, even if there is only one track.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
Drivers checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers giving the right-of-way to others.
Drivers keeping a four-second distance behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers are going too fast for the conditions. Always drive at or below the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give instructions.

questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass when they use a siren or air horn and red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so make sure the way is clear before you move.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn where it is posted.

questions.question: In traffic moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to crash if you:

options.text: Drive a few mph faster than other vehicles.
Drive a few mph slower than other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Match your speed with other traffic on the road (as long as they are within the speed limit). Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot crash into each other. Multi-car crashes often happen when some vehicles drive at different speeds than others.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive the speed limit with caution.

questions.explanation: Slow down at the first sign of rain, snow, or sleet. These create slippery roads. When conditions are poor, safety may require you to drive slower than the speed limit.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake pedal to help the vehicle balance. Steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Over your left or right shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Your blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which of these statements about following distance is true?

options.text: An experienced driver may use a two-second following distance in normal conditions.
A new driver should keep at least a three-second following distance in normal conditions.
At speeds of 40 mph or faster, a four- to five-second following distance is recommended.

questions.explanation: Under good conditions at speeds below 40 mph, experienced drivers should keep at least two seconds of space. New drivers should keep at least three seconds. At speeds above 40 mph, use four to five seconds. Increase your following distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice:

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change your speed and direction slowly and carefully.
Drive the same way you would on normal roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your speed and direction slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make speed and direction changes slowly. Do not use cruise control on snow or ice. Your tires may slip and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: To see traffic behind you:

options.text: Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often. This helps you know where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow line to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Do not cross double solid yellow lines to pass. These lines mean no passing is allowed. You may only cross a double yellow line when turning into a driveway or business entrance.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection. Oncoming traffic blocks your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up when the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for a driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Wait until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear. Make sure you can turn safely before you go.

questions.question: How can you avoid the dangers of drinking and driving?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Tell someone, "No thanks, I'm driving," if they offer you a drink.

questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you start drinking that you will not drive. You can also refuse drinks or call a taxi. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it hard to make safe choices.
